transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-25
Time: 15:00 EDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Kumar (Redwood Product), Evan Martin (Palmetto CTO), Laila Torres (Palmetto Head of Security), Ben Cho (Platform)
Shared: Deck (link): https://redwood.ai/decks/data-retention (shared during call); Security packet: https://redwood.ai/security-pack.pdf

Summary: Quick demo of Console + API toggles for data retention, walkthrough of Optimize suggestions for reducing stored logs, and discussion of private deployment for regulated payment flows.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll do a 30 to 45 minute run, Samira's gonna jump into the console and show the redaction toggles and API flags. Evan, Laila, Ben, thanks for your time.
[00:18] Evan Martin: Yep thanks, and quick note we're evaluating across a few vendors, um, but security is the main blocker. We need to understand exactly what is stored and what's redacted, and, like, auditability.
[00:30] Samira Patel: Great, I'll share my screen. So this is the Redwood Console \u2014 top right you'll see Project: palmetto-prod-sandbox \u2014 and under Settings -> Data Handling we have the request-storage toggle. By default hosted API stores request/response payloads for X days for debugging, but you can set 'Do not store' per-route or per-api-key.
[00:50] Laila Torres: Can you show per-route? We can't have card numbers leave our VPC in cleartext for any reason.
[00:58] Samira Patel: Absolutely. Under Route Settings you can flip request_storage=off; that prevents logs and request/response bodies from being persisted to our logging store. We also have streaming ephemeral logs for immediate debugging that auto-expire after 5 minutes, but nothing is written to long-term storage.
[01:18] Ben Cho: Does turning storage off affect traceability for incidents? We need correlation ids and traces.
[01:26] Ravi Kumar: Great question \u2014 when storage is off we still emit structured telemetry (request id, timing, error codes) to the metrics plane; bodies are nulled. So you'll retain observability without PII. The telemetry ties into tracing (we support OpenTelemetry).
[01:40] Evan Martin: How about PII redaction, like SSNs or card numbers \u2014 is that automatic? Can we define patterns?
[01:47] Samira Patel: We have a couple layers: automatic heuristics that catch common patterns like credit card regexes, SSN formats, and email; plus a custom redaction policy you can upload (regex or ML-based). You can choose to mask in logs, replace with placeholder, or hash. Note \u2014 heuristics are heuristic, so we recommend a custom rule set for high-risk fields.
[02:08] Laila Torres: And if we run in Private (VPC) deployment, does Redwood still process redaction server-side or do we get an option for client-side tokenization?
[02:16] Samira Patel: In Private deployments you can opt to run redaction modules inside your VPC; logs never leave. For Hosted, redaction runs at ingestion and before storage. If you want client-side tokenization we can support a pre-ingest SDK as well.
[02:30] Evan Martin: KMS \u2014 we need customer-managed keys for any encryption at rest.
[02:34] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault/GCP CMEK) and HSM integrations for Private. Keys are never stored in plaintext and we can provide key rotation docs.
[02:46] Laila Torres: Audit logs \u2014 retention settings and export?
[02:50] Samira Patel: Audit logs are separate from request storage. You can set retention windows and export to your S3 or SIEM via an export connector. Audit logs include action-level events (who changed policies, RBAC events) but do not contain request bodies if request_storage is off or redaction policies are enabled.
[03:07] Ben Cho: Any chance transcripts or model outputs leak PII into downstream logs? We've seen hallucinated PHIs in other models.
[03:15] Ravi Kumar: We have quality monitoring and can run evals to catch regression; also output filtering hooks \u2014 you can run a post-processing filter (PII scrubber) before the response is returned or logged. You can route outputs to an internal sink for additional checks.
[03:33] Evan Martin: Sounds good. What's the difference from, say, standing up an internal hosting? We are considering self-host as a reference.
[03:39] Jordan Lee: Self-host gives you full control but you take on operational burden \u2014 tuning kernels, batching, KV cache management, latency SLOs. Redwood Dedicated/Private tries to give you the best of both: you get predictable throughput and the controls you need (KMS/HSM, VPC), while we manage the runtime and security ops.
[03:58] Laila Torres: Can you demo the API flag for request storage off? We need to see an example curl or SDK call.
[04:04] Samira Patel: Sure \u2014 here's the API example: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"...","redwood:request_storage":"off"}' \u2014 note header vs payload option; you can pass storage toggles per-request via header X-Redwood-Request-Storage: off or per-route in the console.
[04:30] Ben Cho: And retention windows \u2014 is that per-project or global?
[04:34] Samira Patel: Per-project and per-route. Defaults are 30 days for hosted, but you can reduce to 0 days (no storage) or extend for compliance with a longer retention if needed, and export to S3 before deletion.
[04:50] Evan Martin: If we disable storage, can we still run backfilled audits for incidents?
[04:56] Samira Patel: If storage is off, payloads aren't stored. We recommend enabling selective logging for a small percent of traffic or for debug routes to allow incident reconstruction. We also support a 'selective capture' policy where you can capture full request/response for a sample rate and aggregate telemetry everywhere else.
[05:15] Laila Torres: What about redaction accuracy \u2014 do you have metrics?
[05:18] Ravi Kumar: We surface redaction precision/recall on the Optimize dashboard and can run evaluations against your sample dataset to tune the rules and heuristics. We'll include example metrics in the security packet.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: I'll pause for a second \u2014 any other questions on redaction or storage?
[05:36] Evan Martin: Timeline \u2014 we need pilot by next month. We want to run 2 weeks of sample traffic against the sandbox with our PII set.
[05:44] Jordan Lee: Great, Samira will set up the sandbox.
[05:47] Samira Patel: I'll demo the redaction policy UI \u2014 you can create a policy, add rules (regex or ML model), pick action: mask/hash/drop, and scope it to routes. Here's an example rule we keep for card numbers \u2014 we apply Luhn algorithm and mask everything except last 4.
[06:10] Ben Cho: Are there any performance impacts when redaction is enabled?
[06:14] Samira Patel: Minimal. For regex-based redaction it's negligible per-request; ML-based policies run asynchronously in a lightweight inference path. For high-throughput flows we recommend precompiling rules and using gateway-level redaction. We'll share benchmarks.
[06:28] Laila Torres: For private deployment where logs never leave, how do we handle model updates and rollouts? We need canary and A/B testing but inside our network.
[06:36] Ravi Kumar: We support canary rollouts in Private, you can have a control plane that orchestrates rollouts but the inference plane runs inside your VPC. We also support automatic fallback policies to a safe model variant if latency or error rates spike.
[06:50] Evan Martin: Ok, can we talk about encryption of logs in transit to our SIEM?
[06:55] Samira Patel: Exports use TLS and can be pushed into your S3 with server-side encryption using your KMS keys. For SIEM connectors we stream via mTLS; we can provide connectors for Splunk/Datadog/QRadar.
[07:10] Ben Cho: Any known gotchas? Like metadata that still contains PII (headers)?
[07:14] Samira Patel: Good call \u2014 headers can contain PII. We surface header-scrubbing options \u2014 you can configure which headers are persisted and which are redacted. Also the agent/SDK can scrub before sending.
[07:28] Evan Martin: About governance \u2014 RBAC and SSO?
[07:31] Jordan Lee: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, granular RBAC roles, and per-route API key scoping. We'll include sample RBAC policies for security review.
[07:44] Laila Torres: For compliance evidence, can you provide logs proving deletion for audit purposes?
[07:49] Samira Patel: Yes \u2014 deletion events are recorded in audit logs with timestamps and who triggered them. We can provide export of deletion events for auditors.
[07:58] Evan Martin: Let's discuss the pilot: we want the sandbox with redaction rules and request_storage off for 1M monthly tokens to simulate user traffic. What pricing/commitment for that sandbox?
[08:09] Jordan Lee: For pilot we typically provide a sandbox credit tier \u2014 we'll follow-up with exact numbers but no long-term commitment for the initial 30-day pilot. If you want Dedicated reserved capacity we'll provide pricing tiers based on GPU units.
[08:26] Ben Cho: Any limitations on embeddings or other endpoints? We use embeddings for fraud models and need retention policy there too.
[08:33] Samira Patel: Same controls apply to embeddings endpoints. You can disable storage and route embeddings through a separate sink. Also you can set to ephemeral mode where embedding vectors are returned but not persisted.
[08:48] Evan Martin: Good. A quick question about PII in model outputs \u2014 do you have recommended prompt patterns to reduce leakage?
[08:54] Ravi Kumar: Yes \u2014 we have a best-practices doc and Optimize includes prompt templates and evals that measure leakage over time; we'll attach that.
[09:04] Laila Torres: Let's talk about timeline and decision makers \u2014 CFO and legal need to see pricing and DPA. Security lead needs SOC2/ISO artifact.
[09:11] Jordan Lee: Understood \u2014 I'll send DPA + SOC2 + ISO docs. Legal will be on the procurement call, we'll coordinate.
[09:18] Samira Patel: Demo wrap-up \u2014 I'll drop the sandbox invite and show a quick live run: sending a request with card in payload with storage=off and redaction rule active.
[09:28] [live demo noise - screen activity described]
[09:35] Samira Patel: Ok here's the request  -> payload contains card number 4111-1111-1111-1111; response returns masked card: ****-****-****-1111 and no payload persisted in long-term logs. There's an ephemeral debug trace for 2 minutes.
[09:52] Laila Torres: Can you show the audit log entry?
[09:55] Samira Patel: Sure \u2014 audit event shows request id, user-agent, route, and that payload was redacted. It does not show the value.
[10:05] Evan Martin: Perfect. We'll need that evidence for legal.
[10:08] Jordan Lee: Next steps recap: I'll send security docs; Samira will provision sandbox and run test with your PII set; Evan will share sample queries and we'll reconvene for infra deep-dive next week.
[10:24] Ben Cho: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[10:26] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional word swaps (e.g., K-V cash -> KV cache) and timestamps approximate.
